query: I have a Figma prototype of our new user-permissions screen for admins. Can you write a usability test plan and tasks I can run next week?
expected_behavior: Reads reference/test-plans-and-scripts.md and uses the test plan template
States the decision, research questions, and testable hypotheses with success thresholds
Recommends moderated think-aloud with 5 participants per segment, separating admins from end users, and a 1-person pilot
Writes scenario tasks with motivation and a clear end state, without UI words or on-screen labels, including a permission-boundary task
Defines full, partial, and failure criteria and time limits per task, plus SEQ after each task and SUS or UMUX-Lite at the end

query: We ran our test with 5 people. Task 1: 4 succeeded, task 2: 2 succeeded. SUS answers attached for each person. What's our SUS and how do I report this to the PM?
expected_behavior: Computes SUS correctly: odd items minus 1, 5 minus even items, sum times 2.5, averaged across participants, and compares to the 68 benchmark
Reports success as n/N with adjusted-Wald 95% confidence intervals instead of bare percentages, noting 5 participants find problems rather than prove rates
Rates findings on the 0-4 severity scale with n/N and quote or clip evidence
Uses the findings report output template with what worked, limitations, and next round

query: No budget for users this sprint. Can you do a heuristic evaluation and accessibility check of these dashboard mockups before handoff?
expected_behavior: Reads reference/heuristics-and-accessibility-review.md and names the persona and primary tasks first
Evaluates against Nielsen's 10 heuristics with enterprise-specific issues and states it is a single-evaluator, predicted-severity review
Checks contrast (4.5:1 text, 3:1 large text and UI components), focus order and visible focus, 24 px target size, persistent labels, color not used alone, and all component states
Cites the WCAG 2.2 criterion for each accessibility finding and gives one concrete recommendation per finding
Lists predicted severity 3 and 4 issues to validate with users in a later round
